method_limits: only top-level keys are asked; a pointer stored inside a row or a nested block is invisible here
the three key names are the ones E464 found; a face that points at another with a fourth name is not in this population
resolution asks the filesystem on this box: an absolute Windows path resolves here and would not resolve on another host, which is why the spelling is published apart

a stem is counted as resolving only when a face file on disk carries that stem; a stem that names a directory leaf or a study (not a face) is published as unresolved and is not evidence of a broken pointer
a reader is recognised through a string constant equal to the pointer value or its basename; a reader that assembles the path from parts is not resolved and is published as not naming the target
the producer of the pointing face is resolved with E464's write-site data flow, so a path assembled by a function call makes the producer look like an outside reader
